findings.title: Consume backup codes atomically
findings.body: The backup code is read and validated from the initially fetched user record, then a separate unconditional update writes the modified array. Two credential requests using the same code can both read the unconsumed value before either update executes, both pass validation, and both receive sessions. This violates the stated exactly-once property and can let an attacker who races a legitimate user reuse a stolen code. Consume the code through a transaction/row lock or a conditional update that verifies the stored value has not changed, and reject the request when that update affects no rows.

findings.title: Backup codes cannot be used in the external-provider 2FA flow
findings.body: The new backup-code branch is unreachable for users entering the `/auth/login?totp=...` flow used after Google/SAML authentication. Before this branch, line 113 rejects every non-CAL identity provider when `credentials.totpCode` is absent; a backup-code submission intentionally has no TOTP code. The login UI also renders `ExternalTotpFooter` for this flow, which provides no "Lost access" option. Consequently, users with external-provider accounts protected by 2FA cannot use their backup codes to recover access.

findings.title: The backup-code authentication and one-time-use behavior is untested
findings.body: The added test coverage only verifies that the backup-code screen can copy/download data. It never submits a backup code through login or the disable-2FA recovery flow, and never verifies that a successfully used code is rejected on a subsequent attempt. These are the primary new authentication and security semantics, so regressions such as codes not being passed to NextAuth or not being consumed would pass the current suite.
